source.title: How Language Models Choose Sides: Internal Representations of Instruction Hierarchy
source.authors: Enrique Balp-Straffon; Chih-Hao Hsu; Rushiraj Gadhvi; Sunishchal Dev; Callum McDougall; A. Mujumdar

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains some flattened or garbled equations and table formatting, but the study and its reported results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures and steers representations of system-versus-user instruction conflict. It does not test sparse-feature superposition, feature overlap, feature capacity, or SAE feature completeness.
record.gate_note: The paper's probe and steering results concern instruction-conflict outcomes, not the feature geometry described in the claim. They are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of V1–V6. Cited claims from other work were not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper probes and steers system-versus-user instruction-conflict outcomes in residual streams of instruction-tuned LLMs. It does not study sparse features, superposition, polysemantic neurons, capacity, SAEs or feature dimensionality. It cites linear-representation work (Park et al.) only for probe geometry, and never mentions superposition. Its probe-direction cosine results concern classifier normals, not stored features.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that models split into hierarchy, anti-hierarchy and no-channel-effect regimes across eight models, and that within Gemma-4 the system-channel effect strengthens with scale. Causal (steering) evidence is limited to Llama-3.1-8B and four conflicts.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not apply the original superposition method; it probes and steers instruction-conflict outcomes in residual-stream activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe results depend on probe method, layer, and activation position; direction geometry differs by method. Steering outcomes depend on direction family, layer, and steering magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: Conflict outcome is linearly decodable from residual streams, peaking at IID-MM BA 0.97 (Llama-3.1-8B), 0.951 (Qwen2.5-7B) and 0.930 (gpt-oss-20b). DiM, IID-MM and LR give near-orthogonal directions (mean absolute cosine 0.022–0.367).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction-conflict outcomes are linearly readable, but equally accurate probes recover geometrically distinct directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean of four per-conflict LR directions at L12 lifts genuine SCR from 0.132 to 0.530 (0.522 with matched projection steering). IID-MM reaches only 0.156, and single per-conflict probes reach 0.11–0.26.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear separability does not determine which direction causally steers instruction-conflict outcomes.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The authors state that causal evidence is limited to one model and four conflicts. The paper also reports verifier artifacts and degraded response quality under some steering settings. The probing evidence is about instruction-conflict outcomes, not superposition.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results on sparse-feature superposition or the claim versions were available to extract; the included rows are related instruction-conflict findings only.

untested.parts: All parts: toy models, sparse features exceeding dimensions, near-orthogonal storage, sparsity-dependent transition, geometry.
All parts: polysemantic neurons and capacity competition.
All parts: non-capacity sources of polysemanticity.
All parts: features spread across neurons, and SAE/dictionary recovery in LLMs.
All parts: SAE feature completeness, stability, canonicity.
All parts. A single steering direction is used, but feature dimensionality is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The paper does not discuss superposition at all; it only cites linear-representation-hypothesis work for probe geometry. T6 stands. Probe-direction cosines (R8–R10 and the Appendix B equivalents) should not be read as feature-overlap evidence. Cross-model cosine values in Table 2 (Qwen: 0.052/0.111/0.334; gpt-oss: 0.031/0.049/0.367) are not rowed, but they are irrelevant to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Sparse features, overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Capacity pressure as an explanation of polysemantic neurons or feature sharing.
Polysemanticity and whether it can arise without capacity pressure.
Feature spreading across neurons and sparse feature recovery with dictionaries or SAEs.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.
